title: Passive Device Layout
intro: Laying out resistors, capacitors and diodes so their ratios hold and their parasitics stay small (Razavi, Section 19.2.6).

blocks.text: Silicide-block poly resistors are linear, have low substrate capacitance and match well (a few-micron resistors to about 0.2%); their linearity depends on length. Ratios should be built from identical units in series or parallel, in the same orientation, with dummies at the ends. A ratio that is not a simple integer is approximated by a fraction of small integers.

The total resistance includes the poly body and the two contact-silicide interfaces. Contacts are tiny (around 80 nm square in 40 nm technology) and poorly controlled, so their share must be small; doubling both width and length keeps the body resistance but halves the contact contribution. Large values are made of short units placed side by side and joined in series, which matches better than a serpentine, whose corners add uncertain resistance.

items: Poly sheet resistance varies by up to about ±20% with process; temperature coefficients are around +0.1%/°C (p+) and −0.1%/°C (n+).
n-well: about 1 kΩ/□, ±40% with process, width-dependent (side diffusion of a deep well), voltage-dependent (the depletion region to the substrate eats into its thickness) and +0.2 to +0.5%/°C.
Silicided diffusion or poly: 20 to 30 Ω/□, only for small, non-critical values (silicided poly varies 20 to 30%).
Metal: very low values, e.g. a ladder in a very fast ADC built as a long metal line with taps; aluminium has about +0.3%/°C, and narrow lines match poorly.

blocks.text: Voltage dependence of n-well resistors: a resistor whose well sits at a higher potential relative to the substrate has a thicker depletion layer and less conducting depth. In a resistor ladder spanning a range of voltages, the units at the top are therefore systematically larger than those at the bottom.

Linear capacitors are stacks of the available conductors: a poly-metal or a single metal pair, or interleaved stacks using many metal layers. Adjacent metal layers give roughly 35 to 40 aF/µm² and poly to metal 1 about 60 aF/µm², so a stack of nine layers is many times denser than a single pair. The bottom-plate ratio $C_P/C$ is smallest (5 to 10%) for structures using only the top layers and grows to about 20% for a full stack. Absolute values may vary 20% in a digital process (gate oxide only about 5%), though a full stack averages the variations of many layers. Fringe capacitance must be added.

blocks.alt: A five by five grid of squares: the outer ring are dummy units, the inner three by three block is eight C1 units around a single C2 unit in the centre.
blocks.caption: A unit array for $C_1/C_2 = 8$ with a dummy ring.

blocks.text: Matched capacitors follow the same rules as transistors and resistors: identical units, common centroid, dummies around the array. Capacitors are, however, very sensitive to wiring capacitance: every top-plate and bottom-plate connection adds some, and in practice the routing always disturbs the ratio slightly.

A junction to the substrate must stay reverse-biased (its anode is the grounded substrate), so it is useful only as a varactor. A p+ diffusion in an n-well is really the emitter-base junction of a vertical pnp whose collector is the substrate: forward-biased, most of its current goes to the substrate. Analog CMOS therefore avoids forward-biased diodes except in bandgap references.

blocks.title: A bandgap resistor ratio
blocks.text: A bandgap needs $(R_2/R_1)\ln n = 17.2$. With $n = 24$, what ratio is required, and how would you build it from identical units?
solution: Approximate by $27/5 = 5.40$ (0.2% error): $R_1$ = 5 units in series, $R_2$ = 27 units in series, all identical, interleaved with $R_1$ in the middle of the array and dummies at both ends.

blocks.title: n-well ladder mismatch
blocks.text: An n-well resistor ladder runs from 0.2 V to 1.2 V. The well is 1.5 µm deep at zero bias with $N_{well} = 2\times10^{16}\text{ cm}^{-3}$ and $\phi_B = 0.7\text{ V}$. Estimate the ratio of the top unit's resistance to the bottom unit's.
solution: Depletion depth $x_d = \sqrt{2\epsilon_{si}(\phi_B + V)/(qN_{well})}$: 0.21 µm at 0 V, 0.24 µm at 0.2 V, 0.35 µm at 1.2 V.
Effective depth (relative to the built-in reference) $t_0 - x_d(V) + x_d(0)$: 1.47 µm at the bottom, 1.36 µm at the top.
Ratio $1.47/1.36 = 1.08$: the top unit is about 8% larger, a systematic error that bends the ladder.

blocks.title: Unit array for gain 24
blocks.text: A switched-capacitor gain stage needs $C_1/C_2 = 24$. Propose an array.
solution: Use a 5 × 5 core: $C_2$ is the centre unit and $C_1$ the 24 units around it, so the centroids coincide. Surround the core with a ring of dummies (7 × 7 overall) and route top and bottom plates as symmetrically as possible.
blocks.answer: 5 × 5 core with $C_2$ at the centre, plus a dummy ring.
